researchSummary: This target keeps ten names on the $7,426 book and changes as little as possible. Eight of them are already held: NVDA 18%, V 13%, MSFT 11.5%, LLY 9.5%, META 9%, MA 7%, NEM 7% and SPY 10%. SPY is only a residual. The two new names are KO 9% and AMZN 6% at the floor, sized down because AMZN reports earnings after the close on Oct 29 at a weaker-than-usual entry. META and NEM come back from phase-out because they passed verification. The weights favour names that score well on several sleeves: quality and growth on NVDA, MSFT and META, payments compounders capped together at 20%, and gold-miner diversification through NEM. The megacap-tech/AI cluster totals 44.5% (NVDA 18 + MSFT 11.5 + META 9 + AMZN 6), under the 48% cap. If finalize-target keeps GOOGL and AAPL as phase-out positions, the cluster comes back under review there. The defensive total is 9% direct (KO, staples), chosen on its verified composite and not as ballast. It is about 18.5% if LLY's healthcare position counts, since its 0.40 range clears the 0.42 vol gate, plus about 1pp held through SPY. Two non-verified incumbents are handled differently. XOM is on its second strike and exits; there is no evidence its thesis is broken, it simply did not re-qualify in two straight refreshes. GOOGL, AAPL, CAT and UNP did not reach the verified survivor set this cycle, so I have no verdict that their thesis is broken. They are left to the churn governor's one-cycle phase-out retention rather than exited on this list. Entry timing is a real concern: MSFT reports tonight, LLY and MA report tomorrow morning and AMZN tomorrow after the close. Their weights are trimmed by each name's entry discount (0.88 to 0.94), not deferred, and the entry zones sit near spot.
